newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasolines ease as buyers exit on lower NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasolines ease as buyers exit on lower NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot unleaded gasoline prices eased in quiet Wednesday discussion as buyers withdrew bids amid a sharply lower futures market, brokers said.
NYMEX March heating oil futures shed 1.01 cents a gallon from sharp morning gains, settling around 60.85 cents a gallon.
The volatile contract scared off West Coast buyers, who waited to see the extend of the market collapse.
Unleaded gasoline deals were heard done early in Los Angeles at 74 cents for February and 75.50 cents for March.
Gasolines meanwhile lost further ground in afternoon trade, with sellers dropping their March offers one cent to 75 cents.
Conventional gasoline in L.A. fell one cent to 70/71 cents a gallon, traders said.
March barrels of gasoline carried the two-cent premium because changes in vapor pressure requirements are expected to result in lower production of second cycle March gasoline.
